**Analysis Summary:**

**Test image observations:**
- Soybean plants in active **flowering stage** (visible purple flowers)
- Several leaves show **interveinal chlorosis** — yellowing between veins
- **Patchy distribution** across the canopy; not all plants equally affected
- Plants appear normal height (not severely stunted)
- No white powdery coating, no discrete dark lesions, no brown stem lesions visible at this scale

**Candidate elimination:**
- **Anthracnose, Green_stem_disorder, Soybean_rust**: Late-season maturity symptoms — not matching flowering stage
- **Charcoal_rot, Phytophthora, Pythium, Rhizoctonia**: Stem/seedling collapse symptoms — not matching
- **Powdery_Mildew**: Would show visible white powdery coating — absent
- **Cercospora**: Distinctive dark purple/bronze discoloration on upper leaf surface — absent
- **White_Mold, Diaporthe, Phomopsis**: Stem/pod-focused with white cottony or black speck signs — absent
- **Bacterial_Pustule, Bacterial_Blight, Frogeye**: Would show distinct angular/circular lesions at leaf level — not visible
- **Soybean_Cyst_Nematode**: Causes patches of stunting + chlorosis, but plants appear normal height

**Best matches:**
- **Sudden_death_syndrome**: Occurs *during/after flowering*, causes interveinal chlorosis (yellowing between veins while midvein and major lateral veins remain green), petioles remain on stem, patchy canopy appearance — timing and pattern match well
- **Soybean_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus**: Can cause interveinal yellowing + mottling, but typically shows wrinkled/distorted, thick dark green leaves

The interveinal chlorosis pattern visible at canopy level during flowering strongly points to **Sudden_death_syndrome**, which is one of the most common and recognizable diseases causing this exact foliar pattern at this growth stage.
